artist.name: Rikith Reddy
artist.bio: I'm Rikith Reddy. I started painting during the COVID lockdown — I needed something that would slow my brain down, and watercolour did that. It still does. I'm a data scientist by day and I paint every day. Most of what you see here came out of early mornings and late evenings, teaching myself from scratch. I work mostly in Daniel Smith watercolours and I've slowly found a style I can call my own.

still-waters.name: Still Waters
still-waters.description: Water showed up in my paintings more than any other subject. These were my most meditative sessions, sitting with a reference, following water over rock, watching it find its own path. Every waterfall here is different but they all have the same quality: movement that looks like stillness.

open-skies.name: Open Skies
open-skies.description: Mountains and high places have always made me feel calm in a way I can't fully explain. These paintings are attempts to get that feeling onto paper, the quality of light at altitude, the colours that exist only above the clouds.

field-notes.name: Field Notes
field-notes.description: I started painting birds because they wouldn't sit still. Every painting in this series is a study in patience. These come from long sessions with reference, working slowly, trying to understand how colour builds into form one layer at a time.

into-the-dark.name: Into the Dark
into-the-dark.description: This style came from a single experiment with a dark background wash. The subject looked completely different. I started adding white ink lines, rain, light rays, geometric patterns, and found something that felt entirely my own. Most of my favourite work lives here.

sacred.name: Sacred
sacred.description: I painted both Ganeshas as a kind of ritual beginning, the remover of obstacles at the start of a new practice. The intention is different from the rest of my work. More devotional than observational.

paintings.title: Forest Cascade
paintings.description: A waterfall coming down through a dense green forest. I painted this when I was still working out how to show moving water without overworking the paper. The trees came together quickly. The water took several tries.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet washes for foliage, dry brush for rock textures, lifted highlights for waterfall spray

paintings.title: Coastal Ridgeline
paintings.description: A mountain ridge dropping to meet the sea. The gap in the clouds above the water was what I was chasing when I started this painting. I kept simplifying until the light was the only thing that mattered.
paintings.technique: Bold wet-on-wet sky washes, negative painting for mountain silhouettes

paintings.title: European Robin
paintings.description: A robin on a dark background with white ink lines spreading outward from it. This was my first attempt at the style I kept coming back to, dark wash first, then the subject on top, then the lines. The red chest against all that dark felt exactly right.
paintings.technique: Watercolour base, white gel pen and ink linework overlay, masking fluid for highlights

paintings.title: Superb Fairy-wren I
paintings.description: The first time I painted a fairy-wren, I had no idea I would keep painting them. This one is straightforward, a bird on a branch against a soft background. I spent most of the session just trying to get the blue of the crown right. It took a lot of layers.
paintings.technique: Controlled wet-on-dry layering, granulation effects in background wash

paintings.title: Superb Fairy-wren II
paintings.description: The second fairy-wren, a slightly different pose with a cooler background tone. I was still figuring out how to handle very saturated colours without them going garish. This one came closer.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet background with salt texture, detailed dry-brush feather work

paintings.title: Summit Lines
paintings.description: A mountain with white contour lines painted over it, like a topographic map laid on top of the landscape. I was thinking about how maps and landscapes describe the same place in completely different ways. The white ink at the end changed everything about it.
paintings.technique: Watercolour base, white ink contour line overlay, wax resist for snow highlights

paintings.title: Superb Fairy-wren III
paintings.description: A fairy-wren on a dark background with geometric lines radiating outward. The lines make it look like a signal going out from the bird. I liked the idea that something small and vivid could feel like it was sending out a frequency.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, white gel pen geometric overlay, masking fluid highlights

paintings.title: Above the Cloud Line
paintings.description: A peak above the clouds catching the first light of the day. That pink and gold moment at sunrise lasts only a few minutes before the ordinary light takes over. I painted this trying to hold onto what it looks like before it goes.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet gradients, granulation medium in clouds, lifted highlights on snow

paintings.title: Red-crowned Cranes
paintings.description: Two red-crowned cranes wading in golden-hour water. This is a warmer and looser painting than a lot of my bird work. The orange reflection in the water tied it together. The simple tree line in the background was a late decision that I think was the right one.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet washes, minimal linework for bird detail

paintings.title: Veiled Falls
paintings.description: A wide waterfall dropping into darkness, with trees and birds around it. The birds are just two small shapes in the sky but they change the whole feeling of the painting. It stops being just a waterfall and becomes a place.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet canopy washes, dry brush waterfall, negative painting for birds

paintings.title: Spectral Owl
paintings.description: An owl painted in every colour that felt right, blues, pinks, yellows, and greens all bleeding into each other. This is not what an owl actually looks like. But watercolour lets you do this, and it felt like a genuinely joyful session.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet colour blooms, salt texture on background, controlled lifting

paintings.title: Rock Pool
paintings.description: A forest stream breaking over flat stones into a quiet pool below. I love painting the moment where moving water becomes still. The rocks in the foreground were built up in dry brush, and the reflections in the pool were lifted out while the wash was still wet.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet foliage, dry brush for rock texture, lifted highlights for water flow

paintings.title: Sun Conure
paintings.description: A sun conure on a deep green background. The bird's colours are already so vivid that I needed the background to go very dark to give them something to push against. The starburst lines around it came in at the end and pulled everything together.
paintings.technique: Deep wet-on-wet background, detailed feather layering, white gel pen starburst overlay

paintings.title: Fairy-wren in the Vortex
paintings.description: A fairy-wren at the centre of a white swirl with blue ink scattered around it. I was thinking about what it might look like if you could see the energy a small bird generates just by existing. The vortex idea was bold, but once I started I liked where it went.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour ground, wet-on-wet swirl blending, blue ink splatter, masking fluid highlights

paintings.title: Ganesha
paintings.description: The first Ganesha I painted. I started this as a way to mark the beginning of a new practice. Ganesha removes obstacles, and this felt like the right way to begin. The crimson and violet palette took a long time to find.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet background with dark tones, controlled layering for the figure, white ink detail work

paintings.title: Blue Flycatcher
paintings.description: A Tickell's blue flycatcher on a slender branch. The blue of its head against the warm rufous-orange of the breast is one of those colour combinations that nature came up with and painters just try to copy faithfully. The muted background keeps all the attention on the bird.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-dry layering for bird detail, loose wet-on-wet background wash

paintings.title: Alpine Dawn
paintings.description: Mountain peaks catching the first light of dawn, glowing gold and amber above soft violet cloud. The sky burns through bands of rose and cerulean for about four minutes and then becomes ordinary again. I painted this trying to hold onto that moment.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet sky gradients, dry brush for rock textures, lifted highlights on snow

paintings.title: Fighting Fish I
paintings.description: A teal Siamese fighting fish against a dark background with white lines radiating outward. These fish are built entirely for display, every fin and colour is meant to be seen. The lines around it felt like the right way to show that.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, wet-on-wet fish washes, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Fighting Fish II
paintings.description: The second fighting fish, this time in red and orange instead of teal. Same approach, different mood. The warm colours feel more aggressive than the cool ones even though the fish are doing exactly the same thing.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, wet-on-wet fish washes, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Amber Falls
paintings.description: A waterfall through autumn foliage, warm yellows and greens all pushing against each other. The birds in the sky above were an afterthought, added near the end, but they are what the painting needed.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet canopy washes, negative painting for birds, dry brush waterfall, lifted mist highlights

paintings.title: Jungle Plunge
paintings.description: A tall waterfall dropping through a dense jungle. I wanted to get the feeling that the forest was almost swallowing the water column, the trees pressing in from every side. Getting the green to not go flat took a long time.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet layered foliage, controlled dry brush for the water column, negative painting for birds

paintings.title: Robin on a Post
paintings.description: A robin tilting its head on a fence post. The background is fast and loose because I did not want it competing with the bird. The tilt of the head is what makes this one work.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet background, controlled wet-on-dry for bird plumage, ink detail for eye and beak

paintings.title: The Spine
paintings.description: A mountain ridge with peaks like vertebrae. I painted this on a larger paper than I usually work with and found that the extra space let me breathe into the sky in a way I had not managed before.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet sky wash, dry brush for rock texture, masking fluid for snow highlights

paintings.title: Ganesha II
paintings.description: A Ganesha in blue and gold on a dark background. The blue is a mark of divinity in some traditions and I wanted to paint that quality directly. I spent most of my sessions on the crown and the face. This one felt more like a devotional act than a painting exercise.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet dark background, layered wet-on-dry for figure detail, gold ink highlights

paintings.title: The Colony
paintings.description: A group of fairy-wrens on a branch, with one cobalt male among the brown females. White lines fall across the background like rain. Painting the one vivid blue bird among all the modest browns was the part I enjoyed most.
paintings.technique: Dark wet-on-wet background, detailed dry-brush bird work, white gel pen rain-line overlay

paintings.title: The Gorge
paintings.description: A river canyon from above, with water threading through the valley far below. The scale was what I was after, that feeling of looking down into something very old and very deep. I kept the colours muted so the depth could do the work.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet foliage and river, dry brush for rock faces, negative painting for canyon depth

paintings.title: Sacred Lotus
paintings.description: A lotus floating in darkness with white lines radiating from it. The lotus has been painted by a thousand painters, but I wanted to do it in my own way: dark background, carefully detailed petals, and lines spreading outward as if the flower is emitting something.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, layered wet-on-dry petal work, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Betta Vortex
paintings.description: Two betta fish spiralling around each other, one orange, one violet. I could not decide while painting it whether they were fighting or dancing, so I left that open. The spiral in the water was the hardest thing to get right.
paintings.technique: Dark wet-on-wet background, swirl blending for vortex, layered fish detail, white gel pen highlights

paintings.title: Macaw in Flight
paintings.description: A macaw mid-flight with its wings spread and its yellow belly showing. The dark background makes the colours pop in a way that white paper never could. The lines around it are meant to show motion and the feeling of air being displaced.
paintings.technique: Dark watercolour background, detailed wet-on-dry feather layering, white gel pen radiating line overlay

paintings.title: Cat in the Garden
paintings.description: A black and white cat looking out through green foliage. The leaves are fast and loose. The cat's face is careful and deliberate. The cat's gaze is the whole painting.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet foliage, controlled dry-brush for cat fur detail, ink linework for face and eyes

paintings.title: Bumblebee
paintings.description: A bumblebee against a soft lavender background with honeycomb patterns in white ink in the corners. I spent more time on the fur texture than on anything else I had painted up to that point. A bumblebee is basically a fuzzy sphere and that turns out to be harder than it sounds.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet lavender background, detailed dry-brush fur texture, white gel pen honeycomb overlay

paintings.title: Robin in the Garden
paintings.description: A robin facing straight at you. Straight-on is harder than three-quarter because there is nowhere to hide if the proportions are wrong. The background is loose and I kept it that way to give all the attention to the bird.
paintings.technique: Loose wet-on-wet background, wet-on-dry breast layering, ink linework for eye and beak detail

paintings.title: Valley of the Spire
paintings.description: A rocky pinnacle above a wide valley. I painted this wanting to capture the feeling of a very large space, the open sky, the distant hills, the valley floor far below. The small waterfall in the foreground gives your eye somewhere to land before you look up.
paintings.technique: Bold wet-on-wet sky and mountain washes, dry brush for rock and meadow detail, controlled waterfall rendering

paintings.title: Robin in the Rain
paintings.description: A robin on a bare branch in the rain. The diagonal white lines for rain were something I had been wanting to try. The robin's warm orange chest against all that cold blue-grey felt like the right subject to try it with.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet dark background, detailed bird layering, white gel pen rain-line overlay

paintings.title: Dance in the Rain
paintings.description: A woman spinning in the rain, her dress billowing out around her. The violet background and the white rain lines were laid down first. The figure came last. This is the only painting I have with a person in it, and I like that it is this one.
paintings.technique: Wet-on-wet violet background, loose figure rendering, white gel pen rain-line overlay, lifted reflections in puddle

paintings.title: Highland Cascade
paintings.description: A river crossing a highland plateau before dropping as a waterfall. This one was painted in acrylic rather than watercolour, which let me keep the greens brighter than I usually manage. The open sky and the wide plateau give it a different feeling from my other landscape work.
paintings.technique: Bold wet sky and hill painting, dry brush for plateau and rock texture, controlled waterfall rendering
